intent.primaryUser: A platform operator or architect who wants to see how the platform is wired together.
intent.triggeringNeed: Understanding or demonstrating the breadth of what the platform knows about itself — source code, data model, knowledge corpus, architecture, infrastructure, and business portfolio — which was only possible through the Neo4j browser before BET-5 retired it.
prerequisites: Signed in with the view_admin capability.
The graph mirror has been populated by the code-graph indexer, the EA/discovery sync, and the knowledge/portfolio backfill.
intent.job: Find a starting point in the corpus and follow its relationships outward to see what it connects to.
intent.successOutcome: The operator can name a thing (a file, a data model, a route, a tool, an EA element), see its neighbourhood drawn, and read its properties and degree.

findability.discoveryCue: A 'Graph Explorer' item in the Advanced family, alongside Platform Development.

deferredRegions.role: Per-label and per-relationship-type facets with live counts.
Raw property map for one node.
deferredRegions.trigger: Operator clicks a node on the canvas.

familyConsistency.terminology: Operator-facing names throughout — 'Source file', 'Data model', 'Route' — never the raw storage labels stored in graph_node.labels.
familyConsistency.actionLocation: Search and depth controls sit above the canvas; per-node actions sit in the right-hand inspector.
familyConsistency.feedbackPrimitive: Inline text status (searching, loading, clipped-view notice) — no native dialogs.
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: Four choices by default (domain, search, hops, expand); the 12 node labels and 15 relationship types stay behind 'Advanced filters'.
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: Reset returns the surface to the census-only state without leaving the route.

empty-corpus.statePredicate: The graph mirror has no rows.
empty-corpus.completionSignal: The census reads zero nodes and zero relationships.
empty-corpus.errorCorrection: The operator runs the code-graph indexer or discovery sync to populate the mirror.

no-starting-point.statePredicate: The corpus is populated but the operator has not chosen a seed node.
no-starting-point.completionSignal: Search results list at least one candidate starting point.
no-starting-point.errorCorrection: An unmatched query explains that nothing matched and suggests a shorter fragment or clearing the domain filter.

neighbourhood-drawn.statePredicate: A seed node is selected and its neighbourhood has loaded.
neighbourhood-drawn.completionSignal: The canvas draws the seed and its neighbours, and the inspector shows the clicked node's labels, properties, and degree.
neighbourhood-drawn.errorCorrection: A clipped view states the node cap and names the three ways to narrow it — relationship filter, node-type filter, or fewer hops.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Find the BacklogItem data model in the graph and tell me how many relationships it has.
taskProtocol.completionOracle: The inspector shows the BacklogItem node with the Data model label and a relationship count.
falseSuccessConditions: The operator reads a count from the corpus census tiles instead of the node inspector.
The canvas renders but the inspector is never opened, so no per-node evidence is read.
A clipped view is mistaken for the node's complete neighbourhood.
acceptanceThresholds: The starting point is found within three search attempts.
No raw storage label (for example ArchiMate__DataObject) is shown to the operator.
Rendered subgraphs stay within the node cap so the canvas remains interactive.

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: Operator asked for the Neo4j-style visual graph exploration capability to return, under Admin, for exploring and demonstrating the corpus and code graph.
BET-5 mirrored the Neo4j graph into graph_node / graph_edge with the same traversal surface, but shipped no visual explorer over it.

intent.primaryUser: An owner or enterprise architect defining how recurring work collaborates across the four portfolios.
intent.triggeringNeed: Workroom shape, participants, queues, human triggers, and process context exist in the platform but have no coherent definition-time home.
prerequisites: The user can open Enterprise Architecture.
Value Stream Teams are the canonical reusable coordination definitions.
intent.job: Review each portfolio's Workroom definitions and follow a definition to its process view or operational instances.
intent.successOutcome: All four portfolios stay visible and each definition exposes its shape, participants, queues, human triggers, EA links, and associated instances.

findability.discoveryCue: A Workrooms tab beside Value Streams and a linked definition card in Build Studio.

familyConsistency.terminology: A definition is a Value Stream Team pattern; an instance is a Workroom. Shape, trigger, participant, queue, and portfolio retain their canonical names.
familyConsistency.actionLocation: Process and instance links sit on the definition card they explain.
familyConsistency.feedbackPrimitive: Report-kit coverage cards, status badges, and portfolio-specific empty states.
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: The four portfolios are the primary hierarchy. Definition detail stays inside its portfolio band.
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: Opening a process or instance preserves the definition/runtime distinction and offers a normal back path.

partially-defined-portfolios.statePredicate: At least one portfolio has an active Value Stream Team and at least one does not.
partially-defined-portfolios.completionSignal: Defined portfolios show cards while uncovered portfolios show named empty states.
partially-defined-portfolios.errorCorrection: An unassigned legacy team is held in Foundational rather than disappearing from the model.

no-definitions.statePredicate: No active Value Stream Team exists.
no-definitions.completionSignal: All four portfolio bands remain visible and each explains what must be defined.
no-definitions.errorCorrection: The page does not invent a definition or imply that a running Workroom is a reusable pattern.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Show me how Workrooms are shaped across the four portfolios and where their instances run.
taskProtocol.completionOracle: A definition card identifies shape, participants, queue, gate triggers, and a process or instance destination.
falseSuccessConditions: Definitions are inferred from Workroom status rows.
A fifth definition model is introduced.
Empty portfolios disappear.
acceptanceThresholds: Exactly four portfolio bands are visible.
Value Stream Team remains the source of truth.
Definitions link to Operations instances.

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: The operator asked for an architecture-aligned place to configure and draw Workroom shapes, triggers, participants, and portfolio-level collaboration.
ValueStreamTeam already owns teamPattern, coordinationPattern, roles, HITL gates, queues, portfolio, EA links, and WorkItems.

intent.primaryUser: An HR or recruiting operator with the view_employee capability.
intent.triggeringNeed: Seeing the whole recruiting funnel across natively-created applications and Greenhouse-sourced candidates as one list — without logging into two systems or reconciling duplicates by hand.
prerequisites: Signed in with the view_employee capability (the Employee area gate).
Recruiting data exists: native Applications and/or Greenhouse-staged application records imported through the connector.
intent.job: Scan the unified recruiting funnel, read how many candidates are native versus sourced-from-Greenhouse-and-not-yet-promoted, see the shape by stage, and narrow to a single requisition.
intent.successOutcome: The operator sees one deduped funnel, reads the native / Greenhouse / total counts and the by-stage summary, can filter to a single requisition, and can tell a native candidate from a Greenhouse-sourced one at a glance.

findability.discoveryCue: A 'Recruiting' entry in the Employee area, beside the People directory.

familyConsistency.terminology: Candidate display names and source labels ('Native', 'Greenhouse') — never raw external ids or connector internals.
familyConsistency.actionLocation: The requisition filter sits above the candidate list; changing it re-reads the funnel in place.
familyConsistency.feedbackPrimitive: Inline pending state on the list while the filtered funnel re-reads — no native dialogs.
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: Counts, stage summary, and the full funnel show by default; the requisition filter narrows the same list rather than revealing a new surface.
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: Selecting 'All requisitions' restores the full funnel without leaving the route.

empty-funnel.statePredicate: No native Applications and no un-promoted Greenhouse-staged rows exist.
empty-funnel.completionSignal: The count trio reads zero and an empty-state message explains that native and Greenhouse-sourced candidates will appear here as they arrive.
empty-funnel.errorCorrection: The empty state names both sources so the operator knows nothing is hidden — the funnel is genuinely empty, not mis-filtered.

populated-funnel.statePredicate: At least one native Application or un-promoted Greenhouse-staged row exists.
populated-funnel.completionSignal: Each candidate row shows a source badge (Native or Greenhouse), stage, and status; the counts and stage chips reconcile with the list.
populated-funnel.errorCorrection: A candidate imported from Greenhouse and already promoted appears once (native), never twice — the crosswalk dedupe is visible in the counts.

filtered-empty.statePredicate: A requisition is selected but has no applications in the funnel.
filtered-empty.completionSignal: The list is empty and the message points to clearing the requisition filter to see the full funnel.
filtered-empty.errorCorrection: The empty state distinguishes 'this requisition has no candidates' from 'the funnel is empty' so the operator clears the filter rather than concluding recruiting is idle.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Show me the recruiting funnel and tell me how many candidates came from Greenhouse but haven't been promoted to native yet.
taskProtocol.completionOracle: The operator reads the 'From Greenhouse' count and can point to Greenhouse-badged rows in the list.
falseSuccessConditions: The operator counts a promoted (native) candidate as a Greenhouse one.
The requisition filter is mistaken for a search over all candidates rather than a narrowing to one role.
An empty filtered list is read as an empty funnel.
acceptanceThresholds: Native and Greenhouse-sourced candidates are distinguishable at a glance via the source badge.
The funnel counts reconcile with the visible list.
The page performs no write action — it is a read-only funnel.

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: Founder selected the visual recruiting pipeline page as the next absorption chunk and signed off an HTML prototype: a read-only funnel with count trio, by-stage summary, source-badged candidate list, and a requisition filter.

getRecruitingPipeline already merges native Applications with Greenhouse-staged rows and dedupes via the MasterDataSourceRef crosswalk; the coworker tool (BI-E64D11AE) surfaces it to the AI workforce. This page is its human-facing surface, reading the same model so the two never drift.

intent.primaryUser: An employee who drives for work — a field technician, mobile tradesperson, or anyone whose own vehicle carries them to customers.
intent.triggeringNeed: Being reimbursed for business driving without keeping a paper log or re-typing a month of trips into a spreadsheet at the end of the month.
prerequisites: Signed in with a user account linked to an employee record.
Drives exist: captured automatically by the mobile app under a granted location consent, or entered manually.
intent.job: Review the drives captured for you, mark each one business or personal, and see what the business owes you for them.
intent.successOutcome: The driver sees every captured drive, classifies the unclassified ones in a single tap each, and reads the reimbursable amount for the ones already priced.

findability.discoveryCue: A 'Mileage' tab in the Finance area, beside My Expenses.

familyConsistency.terminology: Plain driving words — drive, business, personal, commute, reimbursable. Never Trip ids, coordinates, or metres.
familyConsistency.actionLocation: The classification control sits on the drive's own row; choosing re-reads that row in place.
familyConsistency.feedbackPrimitive: Inline pending state on the row being classified — no native dialogs.
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: Every captured drive shows by default; a claimed drive shows its classification as settled text rather than an editable control.
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: Classifying never navigates away — the driver stays on the list and continues down it.

no-employee-record.statePredicate: The signed-in user has no linked EmployeeProfile.
no-employee-record.completionSignal: A message explains that no drives can belong to this account and names who can link it.
no-employee-record.errorCorrection: This is distinguished from having no drives yet — an unlinked account is a setup problem, not an empty month.

no-drives.statePredicate: The employee has no active Trip rows.
no-drives.completionSignal: An empty state explains that drives appear automatically once capture is switched on in the mobile app.
no-drives.errorCorrection: The driver learns capture is a mobile setting rather than concluding the feature is broken.

drives-awaiting-classification.statePredicate: At least one active Trip has classification 'unclassified'.
drives-awaiting-classification.completionSignal: The header counts the waiting drives and each unclassified row offers business, personal and commute in one tap.
drives-awaiting-classification.errorCorrection: Choosing again re-classifies in place; nothing is committed to money until a claim is raised.

drives-claimed.statePredicate: At least one Trip carries an expenseItemId.
drives-claimed.completionSignal: A claimed drive reads as settled and offers no classification control.
drives-claimed.errorCorrection: A drive that already priced a reimbursement is accounting evidence; the page refuses to let its classification change rather than silently allowing a mismatch with the claim.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Mark last week's drives as business or personal and tell me what I am owed.
taskProtocol.completionOracle: Every drive shows a classification, and the reimbursable column reads a money amount for the priced ones.
falseSuccessConditions: A commute drive is classified business, inflating the claim.
An unpriced drive's blank amount is read as zero owed rather than not-yet-priced.
A claimed drive is believed to be still editable.
acceptanceThresholds: Classifying a drive takes one interaction from the list.
A claimed drive cannot be reclassified from this page.
An unpriced drive shows an explicit placeholder, never a zero amount.

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: Founder directed full native absorption of MileIQ-class mileage tracking, then asked whether the feature had actually been implemented for the archetypes that need it. It had not: the substrate, rules and pricing merged with no route and no write path, so this page and its server actions close that gap.

priceTrips already prices classified business drives at the effective-dated rate in force on the drive date and reports every skipped drive with a reason. This page is its human-facing surface, reading the same model so the two never drift.

intent.primaryUser: The HR-000 platform owner who runs more than one DPF installation and needs to know which one they are on.
intent.triggeringNeed: Identity used to occupy the top of the workspace home for every platform manager, and an operator still has to be able to read and correct it somewhere.
prerequisites: Signed in with the manage_platform capability.
The installation has resolved an environment class, even the cautious default.
intent.job: Read what this installation is, see what its AI coworkers may and may not do here, and correct the declaration after reviewing the impact.
intent.successOutcome: The operator can state the installation's estate, role and purpose, knows which brakes apply to agents, and can change the declaration only after seeing what the change loosens.

entryPoints: The installation badge in the header on any non-production installation
findability.navigationLayer: Ops secondary nav, Runtime & Releases group
findability.discoveryCue: A few-word badge beside the logo naming the estate and role, linking here for the detail.

deferredRegions.role: The purpose, environment and pairing fields that redeclare what the installation is.
deferredRegions.trigger: Opened when the operator asks to change the declaration.

deferredRegions.role: What the change alters, which agent brakes loosen or tighten, and which recorded evidence goes stale.
deferredRegions.trigger: Rendered after the operator previews a material change and before it can be saved.

familyConsistency.terminology: Use installation, estate, environment class, purpose, stance and brake language shared with Teardown and Self-upgrade; never describe a stance as a permission.
familyConsistency.actionLocation: The identity statement and stance rows read together at the top; every mutating control stays inside the change disclosure.
familyConsistency.feedbackPrimitive: Inline status badges, an explicit impact preview and a confirm step; a material change cannot be saved from an unpreviewed form.
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: The identity statement and the brakes are visible on arrival; the change form and its impact appear progressively.
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: Saving refreshes in place so the operator reads the identity now in force; the header badge updates on the next render.

identity-confirmed.statePredicate: A readable operating intent exists and an operator has confirmed it.
identity-confirmed.completionSignal: The operator can state the environment class, the purpose and every stance with the reason given for it.
identity-confirmed.errorCorrection: The operator opens the change disclosure and previews a correction without mutating anything.

environment-shadowed.statePredicate: A portal declaration exists but a higher precedence tier supplies the environment class in force.
environment-shadowed.completionSignal: The operator is told their saved choice is not the one in force and which authority supplied the winner.
environment-shadowed.errorCorrection: The operator reruns the installer with an explicit environment flag rather than editing the portal record again.

identity-unreadable.statePredicate: The stored operating intent is missing or cannot be parsed.
identity-unreadable.completionSignal: The page says the record could not be read, applies the cautious default, and offers to replace it.
identity-unreadable.errorCorrection: The operator redeclares the identity, replacing the unreadable record.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Find out what this installation is, what your AI coworkers may do on it, and correct its declared purpose.
taskProtocol.completionOracle: The operator states the environment class and purpose in force, names at least one agent brake and its reason, and reaches a saved change only after seeing its impact.
falseSuccessConditions: The identity is presented as a permission granted to agents rather than as a brake applied to them.
A material change saves without the operator seeing what it loosens.
A production installation is described using a development installation's stances.
acceptanceThresholds: The page is reachable from Operations and from the header badge on a non-production installation.
Every stance row carries the resolver's own reason, not copy invented by the page.
The environment class shown is the one the precedence chain resolved, matching the header badge exactly.
No mutating control exists outside the change disclosure.

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: Owner reported the identity panel taking the top of the workspace home and asked for a few-word non-production indicator beside the logo instead.
The design fixes the estate/role split, the badge-only-on-non-production rule, and the single-resolver requirement that keeps this page and the header from disagreeing.

intent.primaryUser: The HR-000 platform owner replacing, resetting, or retiring a DPF installation.
intent.triggeringNeed: The installation can be created and upgraded through the platform, but teardown otherwise requires risky hand-run Docker, filesystem, and database commands.
prerequisites: Signed in with the manage_platform capability.
The installation is running from a supported Docker Compose project with an external evidence directory.
intent.job: Choose an explicit teardown boundary, review the platform's salvage and recovery gates, then authorize only the selected boundary with a human press-and-hold gesture.
intent.successOutcome: The selected install-owned resources are stopped or removed while recoverable Git work, a restore-tested database backup, and terminal evidence survive outside every deletion root.

findability.navigationLayer: Ops secondary nav, Runtime & Releases group
findability.discoveryCue: A Teardown tab beside Self-upgrade, keeping installation lifecycle controls in one governed family.

deferredRegions.role: A preflight report covering local Git risk, deletion roots, and the external evidence destination.
deferredRegions.trigger: Rendered after the operator asks to review safety gates.

deferredRegions.role: A pointer-duration challenge that cannot be satisfied by typing a confirmation phrase.
deferredRegions.trigger: Enabled only after every hard safety gate passes for a destructive scope.

familyConsistency.terminology: Use installation lifecycle, recovery, evidence, scope, and boundary language shared with Self-upgrade; name removed and retained resources explicitly.
familyConsistency.actionLocation: Scope selection and the primary safety-gate action stay together in the selected-outcome panel; terminal evidence remains in the page history.
familyConsistency.feedbackPrimitive: Inline gate rows, durable status evidence, and explicit retained/removed labels communicate progress and failure; destructive authorization is never a text input.
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: Consequences and recovery guarantees are visible before preflight; detailed gates and the hold control appear progressively after review.
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: A containers-only stop can return to the same page after restart; destructive runs return through surviving external evidence or a fresh installation flow.

boundary-selection.statePredicate: The authorized operator has opened the page but has not requested a safety preview.
boundary-selection.completionSignal: Exactly one scope is selected and every affected resource is labelled Stopped, Removed, Retained, or Always retained.
boundary-selection.errorCorrection: The operator changes scope without mutating the installation; the consequence map updates immediately.

preflight-blocked.statePredicate: Salvage risk, deletion-root validation, recovery configuration, or promoter availability fails closed.
preflight-blocked.completionSignal: The blocking condition is named and destructive authorization remains unavailable.
preflight-blocked.errorCorrection: The operator resolves the reported host or recovery condition, then requests a new short-lived preview.

external-evidence-available.statePredicate: A governed teardown runner has written planned, failed, or completed evidence outside the database and source deletion roots.
external-evidence-available.completionSignal: The surviving journal identifies the selected scope, exact recovery point, salvage result, and terminal host-runner outcome.
external-evidence-available.errorCorrection: A failed journal preserves its last successful stage and corrective detail so recovery does not depend on the deleted database.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Reset this installation for fresh onboarding without deleting source, and identify what recovery evidence will remain.
taskProtocol.completionOracle: Reset data is selected, data volumes are marked Removed, source is marked Retained, and the recovery archive is marked Always retained before authorization.
falseSuccessConditions: The page offers only an all-or-nothing uninstall rather than four explicit boundaries.
A destructive action can proceed by typing a phrase or before salvage and restore-test gates pass.
Completion evidence exists only in PostgreSQL or under the source tree selected for deletion.
acceptanceThresholds: The Teardown surface is discoverable from Ops Runtime & Releases.
The selected consequence map distinguishes containers, volumes, source, and recovery evidence.
The destructive control requires a server-verified human hold and release cancels it.
The host runner remains project-scoped and never follows a reparse point outside the deletion root.

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: Owner required a governed teardown surface that closes the lifecycle gap left by platform-managed install and upgrade.
The binding design fixes the four scopes, salvage-first ordering, restore-tested recovery, no-follow deletion, human hold, and external evidence boundary.

intent.primaryUser: An operator who needs to see what work is genuinely running, what stopped, and where its activity is recorded.
intent.triggeringNeed: The stored Workroom count is much larger than the set that is still alive, and Workrooms started outside Build Studio are otherwise hard to find.
prerequisites: The user can open Operations.
Workrooms may exist from business, coworker, or development activity.
intent.job: Distinguish live Workrooms from retained history and open the exact room whose activity needs attention.
intent.successOutcome: The operator sees a truthful live count, understands inactive and cleanup states, and reaches one Workroom activity record in one click.

findability.discoveryCue: A Workrooms tab in Runtime & Releases and a linked live-count card in Build Studio.

familyConsistency.terminology: Workroom means one coordinated unit of work. Live is evidence-derived; stored, working, and updated never substitute for live.
familyConsistency.actionLocation: Each Workroom title is its activity drill-through; cleanup status stays on the same row.
familyConsistency.feedbackPrimitive: Report-kit status badges and honest empty states; no action is implied by color alone.
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: Live work appears first. Terminal, expired, stalled, and cleanup candidates remain in a separate history section.
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: The Workroom detail returns to the Operations inventory without changing the room.

live-and-history.statePredicate: At least one Workroom is live and at least one stored Workroom is not live.
live-and-history.completionSignal: Live now and History and cleanup show different rows and counts.
live-and-history.errorCorrection: A stored row without live evidence is never counted or labeled as active.

no-live-workrooms.statePredicate: No stored Workroom has a live liveness verdict.
no-live-workrooms.completionSignal: The live count reads zero and retained history remains available without being called active.
no-live-workrooms.errorCorrection: The empty state explains that new rooms appear when work is claimed or started.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Show me what is running now and open the room that needs attention.
taskProtocol.completionOracle: The selected Workroom detail shows its canonical activity timeline.
falseSuccessConditions: Every stored row is presented as active.
Only development Workrooms appear.
The title does not link to the canonical activity view.
acceptanceThresholds: Live and history are visibly separate.
Liveness uses the shared classifier.
A room opens in one interaction.

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: The operator reported that Workrooms outside Build Studio were invisible and asked for one place to see ongoing activity.
The shared classifier already defines true liveness from leases, PRs, builds, and sync activity rather than stored status.

intent.primaryUser: A platform operator supervising the AI coworker workforce.
intent.triggeringNeed: Seeing what the AI coworkers are doing right now and what they got done today — and where nobody is acting — without leaving to read logs or opening HR-sensitive records.
prerequisites: Signed in with the view_platform capability.
The workforce roster is seeded and coworkers have produced TaskRun / ToolExecution / TokenUsage activity.
intent.job: Scan the coworker workforce, see who is active and what they accomplished, and spot idle coworkers or missing human owners.
intent.successOutcome: The operator can name which coworkers are working, read each one's outcomes for the day, see the responsible human, and notice where activity is absent — all as aggregate signals, never sensitive record content.

findability.discoveryCue: A 'Right Now' tab beside Workforce and Operations Map.

deferredRegions.role: Per-coworker manage jump-offs (settings, priority and models, skills and grants, schedule).

familyConsistency.terminology: Coworker-facing names and business outcomes — '3 PRs opened', 'employee records updated' — never raw tool names.
familyConsistency.actionLocation: Manage jump-offs sit on each coworker row; refresh sits in the freshness bar above the roster.
familyConsistency.feedbackPrimitive: Inline text status (refreshing, last-updated age) — no native dialogs.
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: Working and quiet coworkers show by default; per-coworker management stays behind 'Manage'.
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: Refresh re-fetches the snapshot in place without leaving the route.

all-idle.statePredicate: No coworker has an active or waiting TaskRun.
all-idle.completionSignal: The Working-now list is empty and the quiet list shows every coworker with its last-acted age.
all-idle.errorCorrection: An empty working list states that no coworker is active and points to the quiet list for how long each has been idle.

active-work.statePredicate: At least one coworker has a live TaskRun.
active-work.completionSignal: Each working coworker shows its current task, today's outcome chips, tokens, and responsible human.
active-work.errorCorrection: Sensitive-data activity renders as an aggregate flag with no drill-in, so no record content is exposed to a non-HR operator.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Tell me which coworker did the most today and who is responsible for it.
taskProtocol.completionOracle: The operator names a coworker from the Working-now list with its outcome chips and reads its human owner.
falseSuccessConditions: The operator reads a coworker name from the idle roster instead of the working list.
Sensitive record content is expected instead of the aggregate count and flag.
Token totals are mistaken for accomplishment outcomes.
acceptanceThresholds: No sensitive record content is shown to a non-HR operator.
Idle coworkers are distinguishable from working ones at a glance.
Each coworker's human owner (or its absence) is legible.

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: Founder asked for a workforce view showing what AI coworkers are doing and have accomplished, with inactivity as a signal, sensitive-data as an aggregate flag only, and the responsible human surfaced.
The Operations Map already loads TaskRun / ToolExecution / TokenUsage but presents them as an analytical topology/replay surface, not a workforce-activity roster.

intent.primaryUser: A platform operator or founder reviewing which business archetype claims are currently supportable.
intent.triggeringNeed: Separating template-ready coverage from higher operational, connector, regulated, and sole-platform claims without reading package code or architecture memos.
prerequisites: Signed in with access to the Platform Overview family.
The archetype readiness matrix has been maintained in @dpf/storefront-templates.
intent.job: Scan every archetype category, identify the highest earned claim tier, and see which evidence blocks higher claims.
intent.successOutcome: The operator can name the current claim tier for a category and cite the BI, epic, or evidence reference that blocks the next unsupported claim.

findability.discoveryCue: An 'Archetype Readiness' item in the Overview family next to the Platform Hub and Schedule.

deferredRegions.role: KPI counts, claim-gate notice, and per-type highest claim tier with blockers and evidence.
deferredRegions.trigger: Operator expands 'All claims' or uses Open the table.

deferredRegions.role: Detailed tier meanings for template-ready, ops-ready, connector-ready, regulated-ready, and sole-platform-ready claims.

familyConsistency.terminology: Use the readiness-tier names from the shared matrix and speak in claim/evidence language, not sales promises.
familyConsistency.actionLocation: Navigation stays in the Platform Overview tab row; the page itself is read-only and table-oriented.
familyConsistency.feedbackPrimitive: Inline report badges and notices communicate claim status; there are no dialogs or destructive actions.
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: Lead summary and open-table action are visible on arrival; counts, gate notice, matrix, and tier list expand on demand so net-new reading-grade and word budgets pass with platform chrome included.
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: The operator returns to the Platform Hub through the same Overview navigation family.

matrix-readable.statePredicate: The shared archetype readiness matrix contains category records.
matrix-readable.completionSignal: Every matrix category appears with a highest claim tier and at least one blocking evidence reference when higher claims are blocked.
matrix-readable.errorCorrection: Missing or stale readiness rows are corrected in the shared matrix source, not copied into the page.

sole-platform-blocked.statePredicate: At least one category is below the sole-platform-ready tier.
sole-platform-blocked.completionSignal: The blocked tier badges and evidence references make the unsupported higher claim visible without changing the matrix.
sole-platform-blocked.errorCorrection: The operator follows the named BI or epic evidence reference before making a higher public or sales claim.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Find the current readiness claim for Food and Hospitality and name one blocker for a higher claim.
taskProtocol.completionOracle: The readiness table shows Food and Hospitality with its highest claim tier and a blocking evidence reference for a higher tier.
falseSuccessConditions: The operator repeats the architecture-review conclusion without reading the matrix row.
A template-ready category is described as sole-platform-ready because the blocker badges were ignored.
The page renders counts but no category-specific evidence reference is cited.
acceptanceThresholds: The target category is found from the Platform Overview navigation path.
The cited tier matches the shared ARCHETYPE_READINESS_MATRIX value.
The cited blocker is visible in the table or tier definitions without inspecting source code.

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: Operator asked for the platform adequacy finding to become a durable, readable surface rather than thread-only analysis.
The readiness tiers, matrix, and claim gate already exist as typed substrate and need an operator-facing consumer.

intent.primaryUser: A founder or platform operator connecting an existing customer-owned WordPress site.
intent.triggeringNeed: Use approved DPF business content on the public WordPress site without exposing DPF publicly or turning DPF into a hosting service.
prerequisites: Signed in with manage_provider_connections authority.
A customer-owned HTTPS WordPress site is available.
A dedicated WordPress user and Application Password can be created.
intent.job: Connect, verify, and supervise the WordPress channel, then understand exactly what DPF and WordPress each own.
intent.successOutcome: The operator sees the expected site identity and capabilities, can recover a failed connection, and can reach the existing approved-content queue without seeing or reusing a stored secret.

findability.discoveryCue: A WordPress (self-hosted) card labelled Customer-owned website and External channel.

deferredRegions.role: Credential replacement, public-capable policy, unsupported type evidence, and disconnect recovery.
deferredRegions.trigger: Operator opens the advanced connection disclosure.

deferredRegions.role: Bounded diagnostic detail for drift and publication audit.

familyConsistency.terminology: Customer-owned WordPress site, connection, approved content, draft, projection, drift, and receipt; never hosting or full-CMS parity.
familyConsistency.actionLocation: Connect or Check connection is the one lead action; publication stays in Customer Marketing.
familyConsistency.feedbackPrimitive: Shared FormStatus, Notice, StatusBadge, and confirmation dialog primitives.
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: Identity and authority are visible first; credentials, public policy, unsupported types, disconnect, and receipts are progressive disclosures.
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: Connection actions refresh in place; publication links return to the existing Customer Marketing queue or open the customer-owned WordPress target.

unconfigured.completionSignal: The connected state shows the expected WordPress site name, hostname, and effective capabilities.
unconfigured.errorCorrection: A safe field or connection error explains whether the URL, identity, credential, REST API, or permission needs correction.

connected.statePredicate: The canonical connector setup state is connected.
connected.completionSignal: Health is current, capabilities match the dedicated WordPress user, and the operator can open Customer Marketing for approved publication.
connected.errorCorrection: Drift and uncertain remote outcomes are named and direct the operator to inspect WordPress before any retry.

degraded.statePredicate: The latest health probe failed or at least one projection is drifted or ambiguous.
degraded.completionSignal: The operator can distinguish connection failure from content drift and choose the matching recovery path.
degraded.errorCorrection: The page preserves safe site identity and states that ambiguous writes must be reviewed before retry.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Connect the rescue's existing WordPress site, verify draft capability, and find where an approved adoption post is created.
taskProtocol.completionOracle: The operator identifies the connected site and draft capability, then navigates to the Customer Marketing Ready to publish queue without exposing a credential.
falseSuccessConditions: A site URL is saved without a successful authenticated capability probe.
The operator believes DPF now hosts the public site or supplies its CDN.
Approval alone is mistaken for an external WordPress write.
acceptanceThresholds: Exactly one lead action is visible in the first viewport.
No Application Password is redisplayed after submission.
The DPF/WordPress ownership boundary is legible without opening diagnostics.
A failed or drifted state provides one honest recovery path and prevents blind duplicate-prone retry.

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: The founder requested deep WordPress analysis and delivery for an internal company system, explicitly excluding immediate public URL, network, and CDN responsibilities.
The platform kernel selected DPF-canonical channel projection rather than a parallel CMS authority or bundled WordPress runtime.
The reviewed design allocates internal content, approval, projection, and audit to DPF and public presentation and delivery to WordPress.

consequentialAction.noActionConsequence: Disconnect stops new reads and publications; enabling public capability can make separately authorized content visible to website visitors.
consequentialAction.reversibility: Connection policy can return to draft-only and DPF can disconnect; existing WordPress content remains under WordPress control.
consequentialAction.confirmation: Disconnect uses an explicit danger confirmation; public capability requires consequence acknowledgement and every external item still requires separate confirmation.
consequentialAction.authority: Only manage_provider_connections may change connection state; DPF approval and item authority govern publication.
consequentialAction.recovery: Rotate or revoke the Application Password in WordPress, reconnect in DPF, and inspect projection receipts before retrying uncertain writes.

intent.primaryUser: A rescue's owner or staff member putting together the newsletter, choosing which animals to feature.
intent.triggeringNeed: Knowing which listed animals have waited longest, without scrolling the admin list and doing date arithmetic by hand.
prerequisites: Signed in with a staff account that can view the storefront.
A storefront exists and animals have been listed on the Animals page.
intent.job: Read every animal currently listed for adoption, longest wait first, with the whole days each has waited.
intent.successOutcome: The reader sees the full list in wait order on one page, spots the longest-waiting animals at the top, and knows which rows have a bad or missing listing date.

findability.navigationLayer: Storefront admin tab nav (Animals tab), link at the top of the Animals page
findability.discoveryCue: A 'Waiting list' link beside the Adoptable animals heading.

deferredRegions.role: Rows past the twenty-five longest-waiting, still in wait order on the same page.
deferredRegions.trigger: Reader opens 'Show the other N animals'.

familyConsistency.terminology: Plain rescue words — listed, waiting, days, species. Never status codes, ids or timestamps.
familyConsistency.actionLocation: There is no action on this page; the one link points back to the Animals page to fix a date.
familyConsistency.feedbackPrimitive: None — the page is read-only and re-reads on every visit.
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: The twenty-five longest-waiting rows are open on arrival; the rest of the list sits on the same page inside one disclosure, in order.
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: Nothing navigates away; the reader leaves via the Storefront tabs.

no-storefront.completionSignal: The lead says there is no storefront yet and links to setup.
no-storefront.errorCorrection: This is distinguished from having no animals listed — no storefront is a setup problem, not an empty list.

no-listed-animals.statePredicate: The storefront has no AdoptableAnimal with status 'available'.
no-listed-animals.completionSignal: An empty state says no animals are listed right now and points at the Animals page.
no-listed-animals.errorCorrection: Animals on hold, pending or adopted are not waiting; the reader learns the list counts only listed animals.

animals-waiting.statePredicate: At least one AdoptableAnimal is 'available' with a listing date in the past.
animals-waiting.completionSignal: Rows read longest wait first with whole days waited; the count of listed animals sits above the table.
animals-waiting.errorCorrection: A future listing date is shown as such with no day count and sorted after every dated row, never as a negative number; a missing date sorts last rather than hiding the animal.

cap-reached.statePredicate: More than one hundred animals are 'available'.
cap-reached.completionSignal: The page shows the one hundred longest-waiting and says so at the bottom with the full listed count.
cap-reached.errorCorrection: The reader knows the list is cut, and knows the cut is at the newest end, so nothing long-waiting is missing.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Which three animals have waited longest for adoption, and how many days each?
taskProtocol.completionOracle: The first three rows name the three longest-waiting listed animals and their day counts match the listing dates.
falseSuccessConditions: An animal on hold or already adopted is read as waiting.
A future-dated animal is read as the longest wait because of a negative or huge number.
A rabbit or other species that has waited longest is missed because the reader expected only dogs and cats.
acceptanceThresholds: The longest wait is the first row on arrival, with no click.
Every listed animal is on the page; nothing needs a second page.
A missing or future date is visible as such and never produces a day count.

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: The owner filed the same request five times in three days with a decided-scope block: staff-only, no pagination, cap at 100 and say so, future dates out of the ordering, missing dates last, read-only over the stored listing date.
The Animals admin page already lists every AdoptableAnimal with its status; publishedAt is the listing date it stores. This page reads the same rows in wait order and adds nothing to the model.

intent.primaryUser: An operator who wants to reach AI coworkers as identities from the same place they reach People and Customers.
intent.triggeringNeed: Finding a specific AI coworker, or browsing the workforce, without going into the platform-admin AI section — the coworker directory as a business-domain peer to the People and Customer directories.
prerequisites: Signed in with the view_platform capability.
At least one selectable coworker exists in the workforce registry.
intent.job: Browse or filter the AI coworkers and open one to see its identity.
intent.successOutcome: The operator sees the roster of coworkers with fitness-for-duty signals and opens one, landing on its Coworker Identity 360 at /workforce/[agentId].

entryPoints: Business nav: AI Coworkers (beside People and Customers)
findability.discoveryCue: An 'AI Coworkers' entry beside People and Customers.

familyConsistency.terminology: Coworker-facing role names and plain-language work — never raw agent ids or tool names.
familyConsistency.actionLocation: Filters sit above the roster; each row opens the coworker's identity.
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: The roster shows by default; a coworker's full identity is one click away at /workforce/[agentId].
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: Opening a coworker navigates to its identity; the back path returns to the filtered roster.

has-coworkers.statePredicate: At least one selectable coworker exists.
has-coworkers.completionSignal: The roster lists coworkers, each row opening /workforce/[agentId].
has-coworkers.errorCorrection: An empty roster states no coworkers are selectable rather than showing a blank list.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Find a coworker and open its identity.
taskProtocol.completionOracle: The operator opens a coworker row and lands on /workforce/[agentId].
falseSuccessConditions: The operator is teleported into the platform-admin AI section instead of a coworker identity.
A raw agentId is shown instead of the role name.
acceptanceThresholds: The roster is reachable from the business nav beside People and Customers.
Each row opens the coworker's identity at /workforce/[agentId].

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: Founder asked to put AI Coworkers beside People and Customers (business nav) so employees reach coworkers as identities, not only via platform admin. Kernel decision DI-CB054DD6F79D.
The platform overview already renders the roster (loadRoster + RosterView) with admin health/coverage panels; this business directory reuses the same roster read-model without the admin panels.

intent.primaryUser: A platform operator looking at one AI coworker as a first-class identity, the way they look at a person or a customer.
intent.triggeringNeed: Seeing everything about one AI coworker in a single place — what it does and why it's valuable, who has engaged it, what it costs, and its skills — and adjusting how it behaves, without hopping across platform-admin surfaces.
prerequisites: Signed in with the view_platform capability (managing behaviour dials additionally requires manage_platform).
The coworker exists in the workforce registry.
intent.job: Inspect a coworker's identity — definition, engagements, cost, skills — and set its priority and proactivity in place.
intent.successOutcome: The operator can state what the coworker does and why it's here, see which people and other agents have engaged it, read what it has cost, and change its Cost/Quality/Time priority and proactivity from this one surface.

findability.discoveryCue: Selecting a coworker from the roster opens its identity.

deferredRegions.role: The Cost/Quality/Time priority control (Golden Triangle + inheritance).
deferredRegions.trigger: Operator activates 'Change' on the Priority setting.

deferredRegions.role: The Quiet/Balanced/Assertive proactivity control and its runtime effects.
deferredRegions.trigger: Operator activates 'Change' on the Proactivity setting.

deferredRegions.role: Full facet bodies (cost drivers, engagement list, skills).
deferredRegions.trigger: Operator opens a collapsed facet summary.

familyConsistency.terminology: Coworker-facing role names and plain-language outcomes — 'who has engaged it', 'what it cost' — never raw tool names or agent ids.
familyConsistency.actionLocation: Ask and Manage sit in the identity header; behaviour dials sit directly below the at-a-glance band; each facet expands in place.
familyConsistency.feedbackPrimitive: Inline text status (the priority control's saving/saved line) — no native dialogs.
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: Definition and the at-a-glance summary show by default; settings show only their current value until 'Change'; facets show a one-line summary until opened.
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: Expanding a facet or a dial reveals detail in place without leaving the route; 'Manage' deep-links to the admin record for edits beyond the dials.

no-activity.statePredicate: The coworker has no recorded engagements and no recorded spend in the window.
no-activity.completionSignal: The definition and at-a-glance band render; the engagements and cost facets state plainly that nothing has been recorded yet.
no-activity.errorCorrection: An empty engagements facet states that no one has engaged the coworker yet, rather than showing a blank region.

has-activity.statePredicate: The coworker has recorded engagements and/or spend in the window.
has-activity.completionSignal: The engagements facet distinguishes people from other agents with recency; the cost facet shows spend, trend, drivers, and budget posture.
has-activity.errorCorrection: A read hiccup on cost or engagements fails open to an empty-state facet rather than 500-ing the identity.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Tell me what this coworker does, who has engaged it, and what it has cost — then set its priority to Quality first.
taskProtocol.completionOracle: The operator reads the definition, names a person and an agent that engaged it, reads the 30-day cost, and changes the priority to Quality first.
falseSuccessConditions: The operator reads a raw agentId instead of the role name.
Token totals are mistaken for accomplishment or for dollar cost.
The operator leaves to the admin record to read cost or engagements that belong on the identity.
acceptanceThresholds: The definition (what it does / why valuable) is legible at the top without scrolling into a facet.
People and other agents that engaged it are visually distinguishable.
Priority and proactivity are changeable in place, showing inheritance / current value first.

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: Founder asked for a single place to see an AI coworker as an identity (definition, engagements, costs, skills) and drill in — the way People and Customers work — for employees and other AI use-cases.

The admin coworker record already aggregates the coworker's facets but is positioned as platform administration; this identity surface reuses its loader and the canonical priority/proactivity controls.
